name: Nadi Town
tagline: The working centre, cheap and entirely local
description: The main street and market area, busy with shops, Indo-Fijian curry houses and the Sri Siva Subramaniya temple at the southern end. It is a functional Fijian town rather than a resort, which means the prices are local and the food is the best value on the island.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone who wants to eat where Fijians eat
pros: The cheapest food and shopping in the area
The temple and the market are here
cons: Hot, dusty and short on shade
Very little to do after dark

name: Martintar
tagline: Between town and airport, where the bars are
description: The strip along Queens Road between Nadi Town and the airport, with most of the area's bars, restaurants and mid-range accommodation. It is where people staying more than a night tend to end up, and it is the only part of Nadi with any evening life.
bestFor: Anyone in Nadi for a stretch rather than a single night
pros: The area's bars and restaurants are here
cons: On a busy main road with traffic noise
Aircraft noise depending on the block

name: Denarau Island
tagline: The resort strip and the marina
description: A developed island connected by a short bridge, holding most of the international resorts, a golf course and the marina where the island catamarans leave from. It is entirely self-contained and has almost no relation to the rest of Nadi, which is the point for some visitors.
bestFor: Anyone wanting resort infrastructure and the island ferries at the door
pros: Best internet and facilities in the area
Port Denarau marina for island transfers
cons: By far the most expensive part of Nadi
Artificial and cut off from Fijian life
The beach here is grey and unremarkable

name: Wailoaloa Beach
tagline: Budget beach accommodation near the airport
description: A stretch of dark-sand beach west of Martintar with a cluster of hostels, small hotels and beach bars, popular with backpackers heading out to the Yasawas. Sunsets here are the best in the area and prices are a fraction of Denarau across the water.
bestFor: Budget travellers who want to be on the water
pros: Good sunsets and a relaxed bar scene
Easy transfers to the island boats
cons: Dark sand and murky water for swimming
Aircraft noise from the flight path
Very little beyond the accommodation strip

name: Sabeto Valley
tagline: Rural, inland and the cheapest option
description: The valley northeast of the airport towards the Sleeping Giant hills, with the mud pools and hot springs, the orchid garden and a scattering of guesthouses among sugar cane farms. It is quiet, rural and much cheaper than anywhere on the coast.
bestFor: Long stays on a budget with a vehicle
pros: Hot springs and the Sleeping Giant garden nearby
cons: Internet is weaker than on the coast
Cane burning in the harvest season affects the air
